text:
Maria: Heads up — saw a 2x p99 spike on /v1/rerank embeddings yesterday during the nightly regression run. Appears correlated with increased small-payload QPS (200rps, payload ~1.5KB).
Aj: Oof. Was that on the replay harness or synthetic Poisson load?
Maria: Replay harness. We replayed a 48h customer trace scaled 3x.
Sylvia: Quick note: the runtime picked auto-kernel-v1 for the matmul path under that batch distribution. When batches were mostly size 1-4 the chosen kernel has worse tail behavior.
Dominic: Can you paste the perf numbers? p50/p95/p99?
Maria: Sure — baseline (auto-kernel-v1, KV cold): p50 12ms, p95 88ms, p99 320ms. After swapping to kernel-cuda-fused (manual) p50 11ms, p95 46ms, p99 120ms.
PerfBot: Profiling snippet: top time spent in matmul_fused (62%), memcpy (18%), kv_cache_lookup (12%), other (8%). KV miss rate ~13% during the spike window.
Aj: Looks like two interacting factors: small payloads -> tiny batches -> kernel selection picks a generic kernel; plus KV misses causing latency amplification for the few requests that do cache warmups.
Sylvia: Agreed. My hypothesis: auto-kernel heuristic weights throughput over tail by default. For small-batch workloads we should bias it towards low-latency kernels.
Dominic: Proposed triage plan: 1) run a like-for-like (replay) comparison with kernel policy forced to latency-first, 2) run synthetic Poisson with same mean and variance to validate, 3) test KV warm vs cold. Also capture flamegraphs and sampler traces.
Maria: I ran step 1 locally: forced policy -> kernel-auto-v2-latency: p99 drops to 95ms but p95 similar to fused. However cost goes up ~8% (more kernel launches).
EngBench: Synthetic Poisson result (scale 3x, mean 200rps, CV=1.6): p50 13ms, p95 60ms, p99 140ms with kernel-auto-v2-latency and KV warm. When KV cold p99 spikes to ~380ms.
Sylvia: That confirms KV is amplifying the tail. Two mitigations: 1) prefetch/seed KV for replayed queries, 2) increase adaptive-window heuristic to allow more microbatching for tiny requests.
Aj: For adaptive-window, what did we use? current config: max_window_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=1024. If we increase window to 18ms we might get more aggregation without increasing median. Can we simulate that?
Maria: I ran a quick sweep: window=12ms -> p99 120ms; window=18ms -> p99 78ms; window=24ms -> p99 74ms but p50 increases from 12ms to 18ms. So 18ms looks like a good compromise.
Dominic: Any perf regressions after the recent runtime change? (build 2026.03.02)
PerfBot: Regression check: build 2026.03.02 vs 2026.02.25 on rerank-embed benchmark (768d vectors, batch-target 64): median -1ms, p95 +3ms, p99 +22ms. Stack traces point to kernel selector hot path introduced in that build.
Sylvia: I'm going to patch selector to include a tail-weight parameter and flip default for endpoints marked as "low-latency". Feels safe and reversible.
Aj: Two asks for follow-ups: A) schedule an apples-for-apples run (same seed, same replay window) to validate selector change, B) add a KV prewarm step in the replay harness so we can separate cold-start noise from steady-state tail.
Maria: I'll open the benchmark ticket and attach the command lines and perf artifacts. Quick repro command I used: 
```
./bench_replay --trace=customer_X/48h --scale=3 --seed=987 --kv-warm=0 --kernel-policy=auto-v2-latency --adaptive-window-ms=18
```
Sylvia: I'll draft the selector patch and a short feature flag so eng-sre can flip it in staging.
Dominic: Great. If we can reduce p99 by ~50-60% with an ops-safe knob, this should unblock the incident. Also add a metric for KV-miss amplification (p99_delta_when_kv_miss).
EngBench: I'll run the apples-for-apples sweep overnight and post the aggregate CSV. Expecting ~6-8h for full sweep (all kernels x windows x kv warm/cold).
Maria: Thanks team. Next update here after sweep finishes and PRs are up. :thumbsup:
